News.title: Leinster humiliated as ruthless Bordeaux retain Champions Cup crown
News.content:
This time there was no Champions Cup final heartbreak for Leinster, just humiliation. In their previous four defeats at the final reckoning, the Irish province could look agonisingly to key moments when the pursuit of a fifth star fell just short.

But this was different. This time there could be no gnashing of teeth, no looking back ruefully at squandered opportunities. This time they came up alarmingly short against a Bordeaux-Bègles side who have, in the eight years since Leinster won the last of their Champions Cup crowns, established themselves as the new European superpower.

The manner in which they retained their title was, quite simply stunning, with all the damage done in a first half that yielded five converted tries, finished by their outstanding captain, Maxime Lucu, Pablo Uberti, Louis Bielle-Biarrey (2) and Yoram Moefana.

They have not lost a Champions Cup game since being beaten by Harlequins in the quarter-finals during the 2023-24 season. The arrival of Tom Willis from Saracens will only strengthen their hand.

News.title: Uganda confirms three more Ebola cases
News.content:
Uganda has confirmed three more Ebola cases as the burgeoning outbreak from neighbouring Congo continues to spread.

Health officials said the new cases brought the total detected in Uganda to five.

Ituri province of the Democratic Republic of Congo (DRC) remains the epicentre of the outbreak but the World Health Organization warned there was a high risk of the infection spreading to other east African countries.

A week after the outbreak was first confirmed, DRC authorities reported that the flare-up was already the third largest on record, with 750 suspected cases and 177 suspected deaths.

Relief efforts are being hampered by insecurity in Ituri and the fact the outbreak is caused by the rare Bundibugyo strain, rather than the Zaire strain, which caused 15 of the DRC’s previous 17 outbreaks. There are no approved vaccines for the variant, which can kill up to half of those it infects.

News.title: How to get a good night’s sleep when it’s hot and light outside
News.content:
There are plenty of reasons to celebrate a heatwave, but a good night’s sleep is probably not one of them.

You toss and turn, flipping the pillow over and over to try to find the cool side, coated in a sticky sheen of sweat. And the extra daylight is a mixed blessing, making it harder to drop off and trickier to stay asleep once we do.

Light evenings tend to reset our body clock that’s located in our brain. Unfortunately, this is exactly the type we need to feel rested in the morning.

“Our sleep cycle is governed by our sense of light and dark, or circadian rhythm,” explains Dr Guy Meadows, the co-founder and clinical director of the Sleep School app.

The longer we see light, the longer our in internal clock tells our body it is daytime and needs to stay alert. When it gets dark, the body clock signals that it’s time to sleep by releasing melatonin. In summer months we secrete less melatonin, which one reason we wake up earlier and find it harder to drop off.

Temperature is another incredibly important facet of falling asleep, explains Dr Meadows. “Our core body temperature plays an important role in the regulation of sleep. At the start of the night, a 1C drop in temperature is needed to help you fall asleep,” he says. “It’s this decrease, coupled with the arrival of darkness, that informs the internal body clock that the night has begun. This triggers the release of the sleeping hormone melatonin, helping you fall asleep.”

Here, Dr Meadows shares his top tips to sleep in the light and heat:

1. Reduce your exposure to light before preparing for bed

Reducing light use before you head to bed is important, Dr Meadows says. So resist the urge to bask in the evening light.

Draw your blinds to dim the light a good couple of hours before you’re ready to turn in, so that your body begins to step up melatonin production. And don’t forget to switch off electronic devices.

You might also want to invest in blackout blinds – John Lewis do a good range – or at least a sleep mask. Look for masks with adjustable straps that will stay in place and deliver a comfortable, full-blackout.

2. Keep your head cool by keeping a cool head

Dr Meadows adds: “Getting frustrated and restless because you’re too warm only makes your body generate more heat, keeping you awake for longer. Keep cool by lying still and accepting the heat.

“Try focusing your attention on the discomfort and describe what you feel objectively and without judgement, such as ‘I feel heat and sweat on my face, neck and back’. Learning to change your relationship with the heat helps defuse its power and lead to better sleep.”

3. Prepare for cooler sleeping during the daytime

It might sound counter-intuitive, but keeping your curtains closed can stop your bedroom getting warm in the first place, making it easier to fall asleep at night. Another thing to do is to avoid a late dinner.

“Eating food close to bedtime elevates your body temperature, making it harder to sleep,” says Dr Meadows. “For the best night’s sleep, leave at least two hours between eating and sleeping – and limit alcohol consumption.”

4. Wear cotton pyjamas or sleep naked

“If you’re wearing natural fibres like cotton, then you’ll feel cooler in the night than if you were naked, because the cotton will wick away sweat from your skin,” says Dr Alanna Hare, an NHS and private sleep consultant at the Royal Brompton Hospital.

“However, anything man-made or synthetic will keep heat next to your skin. And the same goes for bedding. So if I had the choice between cotton and nakedness, I’d choose cotton. But if you’re choosing between man-made fibres and nakedness, go naked.”

5. Create a breeze

“Sleep with the window open or keep a fan on during the night to add an extra breeze in your bedroom,” Dr Meadows advises.

If you want to keep things extra cool, place a frozen bottle of water between yourself and the fan to cool the air as it comes towards you. (Modern air coolers can chill the room by a few degrees using this principle, although they’re not as effective as refrigerating air conditioners.)

6. Make a ‘cold water bottle’

“Simply fill a hot water bottle with cold water and keep it in the fridge or freezer for a few hours before bed – if you’re an extra hot sleeper, you can leave it in a little longer,” suggests Chris Tattersall, a sleep expert at bedding manufacturer Woolroom.

“Then snuggle up with your ice pack under the covers or leave it to cool down the bed before jumping in – it’s one of the best ways to keep cool at night.”

7. Ditch the memory foam

“The synthetic materials used in a memory foam mattress mean that it’s not breathable and doesn’t absorb moisture, leaving your body to overheat and sweat while in bed,” says Tattersall.

“You know that sinking feeling you get when you sleep on a memory foam mattress? For that to happen, it needs body heat to warm it up, which is then reflected back onto you as you sleep.

“Overlaying your memory foam mattress with a wool mattress protector will help regulate around 75 per cent of that heat, helping you stay cooler on those hot summer evenings.”

Sports.title: Bernardo Silva breaks down in tears in tunnel with wife just seconds before playing final Man City match
Sports.content:
BERNARDO SILVA broke down in tears just moments before his final match as a Manchester City player.

The Portuguese playmaker revealed last month that his nine-year-long love affair with City would come to an end after this season.





Departing City boss Pep Guardiola saw Silva captain his side for once last time for their season-closer against Aston Villa.

And he broke down in tears before even taking to the pitch, welling up in the tunnel before walking out with his daughter Carlota and his wife Degener Tomaz.

Silva was comforted by City keeper James Trafford before he walked out to a rousing reception from the Etihad faithful.

Footie fans around the world were quick to comment on the 31-year-old’s pre-match show of emotion.

Sports.content:
BRUNO FERNANDES broke the Premier League record for the most assists in a season.

The Manchester United skipper has been the club’s shining light in another difficult campaign.





And he capped it off by registering his 21st assist.

Fernandes’ outswinging corner was met by Patrick Dorgu’s thumping header.

And it crashed in off the bar to give the Red Devils the lead away at Brighton.

Fernandes equalled Thierry Henry and Kevin De Bruyne on 20 assists when he set up Bryan Mbeumo’s winner against Nottingham Forest last week.



So when he got the standalone tally, social media went crazy.

United hilariously changed their X bio to: “Bruno Fernandes helped us write this.”

One said: “Living legend.”

And a final user tweeted: “The man of big moments.. he was born for this.”

Fernandes has already been named Football Writers’ Association and Premier League player of the season – and could add the PFA gong, too.

Sports.title: Arne Slot drops huge hint on his Liverpool future in programme notes before emotional Mo Salah Anfield farewell
Sports.content:
ARNE SLOT has given the clearest indication yet that he WILL be in charge of Liverpool next season.

The Dutchman has spent the season taking flak from fans, critics and even his own players, as the defence of his debut campaign Prem title fell apart.





And before Anfield legend Xabi Alonso became Chelsea’s new boss, there was plenty of talk that he would be returning to replace Slot.

Bournemouth’s departing manager Andoni Iraola has also been a red-hot tip to take over.

But Slot has one more year left of his contract and he used his programme notes before the Kop said their farewells to Mo Salah and Andy Robertson to hint heavily that he won’t be following them out of the door.

As he prepared for the clash with Brentford, expected to confirm Champions League football he wrote : “This is our opportunity to take something tangible from the season.



“First and foremost it would allow the club to play in the Champions League for a third successive season.

“This is where we want to be but also where we need to be given the model we have and the opportunities that qualification brings us.”

Slot, who has insisted that he is already working with owners Fenway Sports Group in identifying new players to be targeted in the upcoming transfer window, stressed: “I could not be more aware of what European football – and especially the Champions League – means to our supporters.

“So taking the final step is not something we want to take just for ourselves.

“We also want to do it for you and with you.

“At Liverpool the highest standards are always set for us and by us and not reaching them should sharpen everyone’s appetite for what comes next.”

Slot’s message was accompanied by a far more poignant one from Virgil van Dijk – who revealed that there will “soon be a permanent tribute” to the late Diogo Jota and brother Andre.

Sports.title: Why is Djed Spence wearing a protective mask for Tottenham against Everton?
Sports.content:
DJED SPENCE will be hoping to help Tottenham complete their Premier League survival mission this afternoon – and he’ll try while wearing a protective mask.

Spurs need just a point against Everton to pip bitter London rivals West Ham to that all-important final safety spot.



PREMIER LEAGUE FINAL DAY UPDATES



But a loss would have a detrimental effect on Tottenham’s survival hopes if the Hammers beat Leeds, as there is only a two-point gap between the teams.

However, Spence should be one of the few members of the team in good spirits following his call-up to the England squad for this summer’s World Cup.

And he’ll get to prove his worth to Three Lions manager Thomas Tuchel on the final day of the Premier League season, but the full-back will be sporting a completely new look.

Why is Djed Spence wearing a protective mask?

It was confirmed that Djed Spence suffered a broken jaw on the eve of England’s World Cup squad announcement.



The Tottenham star picked up the injury in the closing stages of Tuesday’s 2-1 defeat to Chelsea.

Spence, 25, was hurt in a tussle with striker Liam Delap as he took an elbow to the face.



The Blues ace was penalised for the foul, but the full-back is still paying the price.

Spence went for medical checks after the match and it was discovered that he had in fact broken his jaw in the challenge.

Djed Spence’s World Cup call-up

Spence was included in Thomas Tuchel’s final 26-man squad ahead of Trent Alexander-Arnold.

He has only made four appearances for the Three Lions – all of which have come under Tuchel.



The former Nottingham Forest star made history in his debut for England against Serbia in September 2025.

He was the first ever Muslim player to represent the nation on the international stage.

Sports.title: Bolton 4 Stockport 1: Trotters seal stunning return to Championship after seven-year absence with Wembley thumping
Sports.content:
SAM DALBY’S wonder strike and a controversial stoppage-time penalty from Ruben Rodrigues sealed Bolton’s return to the Championship after ten years in the lower-league wilderness.

Striker Dalby — who came on as a second-half sub — sent an acrobatic rocket flying past keeper Corey Addai with nine minutes left to put the Trotters 3-1 up.





Then Rodrigues calmly fired home after ref Josh Smith awarded a penalty following a VAR review, where he adjudged that Stockport’s Jacob Dacre-Cogley had tugged Ibrahim Cissoko’s shirt.

It seemed very harsh and Smith decided to send Dacre-Cogley off too.

On a thrilling and hot afternoon at Wembley, Bolton were up and running thanks to Ruben Rodrigues’s third-minute strike,

Although Adama Sidibeh levelled in the 29th-minute and Stockport had Bolton rocking, they produced a superb second-half performance.



Kyle Wootton put the ball past his own keeper in the 64th as he attempted to clear when keeper Corey Addai could only parry an Amario Cozier-Duberry shot.

Then came all the late drama to seal the deal.

VAR is not used in the regular season in the EFL or the play-off semi-finals but it was suddenly used in the final.

And it certainly was not Stockport’s friend as they also saw Sidibeh have a goal ruled out before his eventual equaliser for clipping the heels of George Johnson before running through to fire past Jack Bonham.



BEST ONLINE CASINOS – TOP SITES IN THE UK

But what a day for Bolton and their fans. It’s been a decade of disappointment with the Trotters dropping all the way down to League Two and at one point in peril of going out of business.

They have been stuck in the third tier for five years — losing back-to-back play offs

The heat was on for both teams — literally.

In the shade at Wembley it was 30 degrees Celsius, so goodness knows what it was on the pitch.



Bolton raced into a third-minute lead to raise the temperature.

Stockport keeper Corey Addai failed to deal with a slow 30-yard daisy-cutter from Thierry Gale and parried it into the path of Mason Burstow.

The Trotters frontman pulled it back across goal and the ball found its way into the path of Ruben Rodrigues, who slot calmly into the bottom right corner.

But Stockport responded well and had the ball in the net for what they thought was a leveller.

Sidibeh showed great strength to shrug off Bolton’s George Johnson before running through to fire past Jack Bonham.



But Stockley Park suggested ref Smith go to the monitor to see if he thought Sidibeh had fouled Johnson — and we all know what happens then.

Replays showed Sidibeh just clipped a heel of Johnson and the goal was ruled out.

The Hatters were full of energy despite the heat and were pushing hard for a leveller.

Wootton was unable to generate enough power on a header, which was comfortable for Bonham.

But the keeper made an outstanding save to get down low to keep out a



Josh Stokes effort after Max Conway got caught playing out by Bailey.

County deservedly levelled with a goal of sheer quality.

Sidibeh flicked a wonderful header into the top right corner from a superb cross from Josh Dacres-Cogley.

Jordi Osei-Tutu went for glory as he went on a mazy run leaving Stockport defenders in his wake but his eventual shot was blocked.

Addai had to be alert to keep out a fiercely-hit low Josh Sheehan effort from the edge of the box after being set up by Thierry Gale.



Sidibeh managed to get in behind on the left side after a well-timed run but Conway brilliantly got back to block his cross.

Gale got the better of Dacres-Cogley before teeing up Rodrigues but the Bolton ace saw his effort flash wide.

Wootton had to take a booking for the team as Rodrigues was set to race through from halfway. The Stockport ace hacked him down with a mistimed challenge.

Bolton went back in front after yet another poor piece of keeping from Addai.

Cozier-Duberry got down the right after being played in by sub Sam Dalby.



His shot could only be palmed by Addai and Wootton attempting to get back to clear could only divert the ball into the empty net.

Stockport almost levelled straight away The ball was slid across the box to sub Tanto Olaofe and his shot was kept out by a brilliant Bonham block.

And then Cissoko hit the outside of the post from an angle.



But Bolton made them pay by sealing promotion with nine minutes left.

John McAtee nodded a ball forward into the path of Dalby to acrobatically fire it past Addai to send Bolton fans into bedlam.

Then came all the late drama and controversy. But in truth Bolton deserved this and they are back in the second tier.

Sports.title: What do Chelsea need to qualify for Europa League on final day?
Sports.content:
EUR ON What do Chelsea need to qualify for Europa League on final day?

CHELSEA have endured a poor season by their high standards – but could still qualify for Europe on the final day.

The Blues have gone through three managers this season, none of which will be in the dugout come the start of the 2026/27 season.





Liam Rosenior’s barren run as head coach following the sacking of Enzo Maresca derailed any hopes the west London outfit had of finishing in a Champions League place this season.

Interim Calum McFarlane could not deliver the FA Cup earlier this month, and will be hoping to qualify the Blues for the Europa League on the final day.

Xabi Alonso will have a point to prove in the Europa League, with the final against Atalanta being the only game his Bayer Leverkusen side lost in the 2023/24 season.

SunSport can reveal how Chelsea can qualify for the Europa League on the final day of the season.

What do Chelsea need to qualify for Europa League on final day?

With Man City beating the Blues in the FA Cup final, the final Europa League spot will go to the league standings.

However, if Aston Villa were to finish fifth, then the the teams in seventh and eighth would qualify, rather than sixth and seventh.

Chelsea are in eighth going into the final day, so there are a number of ways they can qualify for the Europa League.

This is what happens if:



Chelsea finish seventh – Europa League

Chelsea finish eighth, Aston Villa finish fifth – Europa League

Chelsea finish eighth, Aston Villa finish fourth – Conference League

Chelsea finish ninth, Aston Villa finish fifth – Conference League

Chelsea finish ninth, Aston Villa finish fourth OR Chelsea finish 10th – no European qualification.

Chelsea are a point behind Brighton, and need to better their result on the final day to jump into seventh.

The Blues travel to Sunderland, and the Seagulls host Man United.

However, both Sunderland and Brentford could finish above Chelsea, should the Black Cats in on the final day, and Brentford beat Liverpool.

Newcastle, Everton and Fulham could all finish level on points with Chelsea in eighth, but their goal difference is a bit too far behind Chelsea’s.

Sports.title: Man Utd star Bruno Fernandes breaks Premier League assists record
Sports.content:
Man Utd star Bruno Fernandes breaks Premier League assists record

Bruno Fernandes has broken the record for most Premier League assists in a season after the Manchester United star produced his 21st against Brighton on the final day

View 2 Images Bruno Fernandes has grabbed a slice of Premier League history

Bruno Fernandes has broken the Premier League record for assists in a season after laying on Manchester United's opener at Brighton.

‌



The Portuguese star had 20 - joint with Kevin De Bruyne and Thierry Henry - going into the clash at the Amex before assisting Patrick Dorgu.

‌



In last weekend's 3-2 win over Nottingham Forest Fernandes equalled the record, leaving him just one game to set himself apart from De Bruyne and Henry. He was on hand to deliver the corner as Dorgu headed home on the south coast.

‌



Fernandes has helped United enjoy a major revival in the second half of the season as Michael Carrick's side rise up to third and secure Champions League football. The ex-Sporting Lisbon star has enjoyed arguably his most influential season, proving to be at his creative best.

Michael Carrick issues message to Man Utd chiefs with talks over transfer advancing READ MORE :

Why are Man Utd wearing a different kit vs Brighton in final Premier League match? READ MORE :

He's topped a host of attacking metrics and they have helped him scoop several individual accolades. Fernandes was named the FWA Footballer of the Year and then backed that up this week by being named the Premier League Player of the Season.

Fernandes is among the favourites to be named the PFA Player of the Year - and that would make him the first United player to win the award in the post Sir Alex Ferguson-era. The Portuguese star, who will be key to his country's World Cup efforts this summer, has claimed that he wants his efforts to end in team titles, not individual prizes.

‌



He recently told Sky Sports: "I haven't achieved everything I wanted. I've never hidden that I want to win the Premier League and the Champions League with the club. I might do it, I might not. But until I get the chance or until I'm here to do that, I'm going to try."

View 2 Images Bruno Fernandes' hunt for the assist record has been well publicised

Since Fernandes arrived in the Premier League six years ago no player has created more chances than him. He has created 670 chances since January 2020, 238 more than City icon De Bruyne who is next on the list.

Sports.title: Michael Carrick issues message to Man Utd chiefs with talks over transfer advancing
Sports.content:
Michael Carrick issues message to Man Utd chiefs with talks over transfer advancing

Michael Carrick has been confirmed as Manchester United’s permanent manager and it appears that planning for his first summer transfer window at the helm is already underway

View 2 Images Carrick has been confitmed as Man United's permanent boss (Image: Getty Images)

Michael Carrick has vowed Manchester United will only sign players that move the club ‘forward’ this summer. The former midfielder is set to oversee his first window as the Red Devils’ permanent boss.

‌



He was handed a long-term contract last week, having impressed in his spell as interim. United have won 11 of Carrick’s 16 games in charge - form that has seen them secure a spot in next season’s Champions League.

‌



With Carrick’s future having now been decided, attention will turn to the summer transfer window. The Red Devils are understood to want to sign a new midfielder as Casemiro’s replacement.

‌



A number of names including Adam Wharton, Elliot Anderson and Atalanta’s Ederson have all been linked. Sky Sports report that a deal for the latter is 'advancing' with hopes a club-to-club agreement is close.

Ex-Man Utd wonderkid backed for huge future set for reunion with Red Devils READ MORE :

FOLLOW OUR MAN UTD FB PAGE! Latest United news and more on our dedicated Facebook page

And Carrick has made it clear that whoever the club choose to sign this summer, they have to be capable of taking the side to the next level.

‌



He said: “I think the beauty of the next transfer window, for everybody, it's always the biggest thing in the world, and the most important transfer window of all time, for every club, I think.

“That's just the nature of how it's been created, to be honest, and I think, again, as a football club, you want to keep moving forward. We certainly do. As a football club, we want to keep moving forward.

“I think it's acknowledged we're at this stage, and the dynamics and the balance of the direction we're at, where we've ended up getting to, and finishing in the league, there's obviously work to do.

‌



“It's quite obvious, with certain players leaving, there's a bit of work to do, but this one is not any more important than the last one, it's what's ahead of us as a football club to try and make the most of it.”

View 2 Images Man United have been linked with Ederson over recent days (Image: Getty Images)

While additions will of course be pursued this summer, Carrick also believes United’s young players could have a big impact next season.

‌



He added: “I've seen that, for sure. I've seen development, a lot of development, in different ways. Some of it you see on the pitch, it's obvious it's there performance-wise, because there's a technical part of it and the players are improving in that regard.

“I think I've said it before, but sometimes the feeling of being comfortable is the best way of being here, knowing what it feels like to play here, having an element of success, having an element of a few challenges, and you come through it and you understand what it takes to get through it.

“I think that, as much as anything, and then you can grow, your character and personality comes out even more. I've seen that for some of the younger players, and actually not just the younger players, you can see everyone grow that little bit more when you're getting good results with good performances.

Article continues below

“So I think leadership's different from everyone. I think there's some leadership examples, some show it a little bit more vocally, but you can definitely see each and every player grow when you're moving in the right direction, for sure.”

Sports.title: Iran to move World Cup training base from USA to Mexico weeks before tournament
Sports.content:
Iran to move World Cup training base from USA to Mexico weeks before tournament

The 2026 World Cup is due to get underway in just under three weeks’ time and despite their place at the tournament now being secure, Iran have made a late decision over their training base

View 2 Images The Iranian national team have moved their training base ahead of the World Cup (Image: Getty Images)

Iran has been granted permission by FIFA to move their World Cup training base just weeks ahead of their first game. The tournament is due to get underway in just under three weeks’ time, with Mexico’s clash against South Africa due to act as the curtain raiser.

‌



Iran will commence their World Cup journey just days later against New Zealand, with their spot at the tournament having now been confirmed. There was doubt that the side would take place due to the ongoing conflict between themselves, the USA and Israel.

‌



And while they will now play, Iran chiefs have announced that they have been granted permission to move their training base from the USA to Mexico.

‌



“All team base camps for the countries participating in the World Cup must be approved by FIFA,” Federation president Mehdi Taj said in a statement.

“Fortunately, following the requests we submitted and the meetings we held with FIFA and World Cup officials in Istanbul, as well as the webinar meeting we had yesterday in Tehran with the respected FIFA secretary general, our request to change the team’s base from the United States to Mexico was approved.”

Prime Minister Keir Starmer's desperate plea in Arsenal Champions League final statement READ MORE :

BBC to ignore World Cup final half-time show as broadcaster sets out plans READ MORE :

JOIN US ON FACEBOOK! Latest news, analysis and much more on Mirror Football's Facebook page

‌



The decision comes just weeks after US President Donald Trump finally gave his blessing for Iran to play at the tournament. He said: “Well if Gianni [Infantino] said it, I’m OK. Did Gianni say it? Gianni Infantino – that’s a piece of work.”

Asked what would happen if Iran won, Trump added: “If they win we’ll have to worry about that. I’m going to have to worry about that one.

“You know what, let them play. Gianni is fantastic, he’s a friend of mine, he talked about it, I said, ‘you do whatever you want’. You can have them, you don’t have to have them, they probably have a good team. Do they have a good team, do you have any idea?”

‌



Trump’s comments followed similar from FIFA President Gianni Infantino. He said: "Of course, Iran will be participating at the FIFA World Cup 2026. We want Iran to play, and Iran will play at the World Cup.

View 2 Images Donald Trump recently gave his blessing to Iran playing at the World Cup (Image: Getty Images)

"There is no plan B, C or D – there is only plan A. Iran represent their people – both those living in Iran and those living abroad. Iran will be at the FIFA World Cup, and we’re excited because they’re a very, very strong team, in my opinion, right now.

‌



“So, I’m very happy. I’ve seen the team, I’ve spoken to the players and the coach. So, everything’s fine. We’re delighted because they are a very, very strong team. I’m very happy.

“And of course, Iran will play in the United States of America. The reason for that is simple, because we have to unite. We have to bring people together."

Sports.title: Precise turns the tables to take Irish 1,000 Guineas
Sports.content:
Precise followed in the footsteps of last year's winner Lake Victoria by leaving Newmarket disappointment in the past to land the Tattersalls Irish 1,000 Guineas in decisive fashion.

Sent off favourite for the opening fillies Classic of the season despite a less than ideal preparation, a lack of fitness ultimately told on the Rowley Mile as Wayne Lordan and True Love stormed to 1000 Guineas glory.

Jettisoned by Ryan Moore who switched to the Newmarket winner and 4/6 favourite for the Curragh equivalent, it proved a different story this time around for the daughter of Starspangledbanner who was the mount of Lordan and sent off 4/1 to add to her impressive juvenile haul.

With True Love following the pace set by Charlie Appleby's raider Abashiri among the cluster on the far rail, it looked like Moore's decision to ride the favourite would prove justified as she hit the front travelling well heading down to the furlong marker.

However, she had no answer to Precise's blistering acceleration inside the final furlong as Aidan O'Brien's charge claimed Classic redemption by two-and-a-half lengths.

Almaqam delivers the goods in Tattersalls Gold Cup

Almaqam registered the top-level success Ed Walker had been craving with an utterly brilliant display in the Tattersalls Gold Cup.

Often left despairing over ground conditions with his star middle-distance performer, who ended last season by finishing third behind Calandagan and Ombudsman in the Champion Stakes, Walker headed into the lion's den of the Curragh for the five-year-old's first outing of the campaign and was duly rewarded.

Sent off 13/2 in the hands of Kieran Shoemark, the bay's rider was bullish from the off as he rolled forward and got his mount in the prime position to accelerate for home in the straight.

Image: Kieran Shoemark celebrates with the Tattersalls Gold Cup trophy

He then advertised every ounce of his class to lead home an all-British one-two-three, with George Scott's Bay City Roller two lengths behind in second and Roger Varian's Saddadd, Almaqam's half-brother, in third.

As well as it being Almaqam's first strike in Group One company, it was Shoemark's first since Friendly Soul's Prix de l'Opera triumph on Arc day in 2024 and a first for Walker since Makarova's Abbaye triumph on the same Parisian afternoon.

As a result of the victory Almaqam is now 6/1 for the Prince of Wales's Stakes at Royal Ascot with some bookmakers.

Walker said: "Kieran was absolutely brilliant on him and has really got to know him. He is a horse who needs waking up and engaging, as he is so laidback. I thought he gave him a peach of a ride.

"Fair play to the horse, as he hadn't run for a long time and he dug deep. It is a sigh of relief too, as I have banged on about this horse for long enough now so it is great to finally do it. People were probably bored with me talking about him and not producing, so hopefully this is his year and we could aim high now.

"This is a seriously tough division and it won't be easy wherever we go but he has bagged a big one now. This is my first winner in Ireland so at least I can come back with some confidence."

Sports.title: Huang makes LET history after Lalla Meryem Cup victory
Sports.content:
Anna Huang made history on the Ladies European Tour (LET) on Saturday, becoming the youngest player in the history of the competition to win three events, after she claimed a one-shot victory at the Lalla Meryem Cup in Morocco.

The 17-year-old, who turned professional in 2025, is competing in only her second full season on the LET, but is already making headlines, with the Canadian coming from six shots back to shoot a sensational seven-under-par 66 at the Royal Golf Dar Essalam Golf Club to outlast Australian Kelsey Bennett with a final score of 14 under par.

Huang got off to a flying start, going three under par through her first two holes, with a birdie and an eagle on the first and second.

Image: Huang has enjoyed a fine vein of form in recent weeks

She backed that up with four straight birdies between holes five and eight, before giving one back to the course with a bogey on the ninth.

She bounced back with a birdie on the 14th and showed her composure to finish her round with four straight pars and, as a result, claimed a cash prize of €67,500 (£58,306) and moved to No 3 on the LET's Order of Merit.

Huang now surpasses Lydia Ko as the youngest player to win three titles on the LET, following her victories at the La Sella Open and Lacoste Ladies Open de France in 2026.

"I'm honestly just so shocked right now," Huang said. "I didn't know where the leaderboard was, and I didn't know where Kelsey was.

"I was just trying to stay patient and make pars in the last few holes. But it ended up being the win for me."

The Canadian has enjoyed a fine vein of form in her last two LET starts, finishing T7 at the Investec SA Women's Open in April and T3 at last week's Amundi German Masters.

Image: Huang got off to a flying start, going three under par through her first two holes

"I got a little nervous on the back nine. I mean, everyone would. But I just kept playing my own game. To get my third win on tour in only my second year is incredible. I'm just trying to enjoy the moment!"

Bennett, who had begun her final round at 13 under, moved her score to 16 under through her opening 10 holes, with four birdies and one bogey.

However, the Australian slumped with seven holes to go, conceding bogeys on the 12th, 16th and 18th holes to finish her round at level-par and the tournament in second place.

England's Cara Gainer, who won the event last year, ended the week at eight under par and tied for sixth. A brilliant second-round score of four under par, which included two eagles and two birdies, propelled the 30-year-old into contention.

However, a final-round score of 71 saw her drop down the leaderboard, with Gainer finishing on Saturday with four birdies and two bogeys.

What's coming up next on the Ladies European Tour?

Sara Kouskova will look to defend her Evian Resort Golf Club as the LET heads to the Evian Resort Golf Club in France next week.

The LET and LPGA Tours will then turn their attention to the second major championship of the year, the US Women's Open at Riviera Country Club in California.

Sports.title: Bolton seal return to Championship after beating Stockport at Wembley
Sports.content:
Bolton sealed their return to the Championship after seven years away as they beat Stockport 4-1 at Wembley.

The Trotters, who had dipped as low as League Two in their time since they were last in the second tier, finally got through the League One play-offs at the third time of asking in the last four years.

Ruben Rodrigues scored their first goal early on, before Adama Sidibeh levelled for Stockport a little while after he had one ruled out by VAR.

Kyle Wootton's own goal restored Bolton's lead in the second half, while Sam Dalby added a third and then Rodrigues scored his second from the penalty spot after Josh Dacres-Cogley was sent off for a hair pull in the box, again given by VAR.

Rodrigues goes from Bolton nemesis to Trotters hero Ruben Rodrigues was lining up for Oxford in the play-off final in 2024, and assisted both their goals in a 2-0 win. Two years later, he scored twice for the Trotters as they won at Wembley.

Bolton overwhelm Stockport in second half to seal promotion

It was some start at Wembley. Less than three minutes on the clock and Bolton were in front. Rodrigues finding the back of the net after Stockport goalkeeper Corey Addai had failed to deal with a fairly tame shot from range.

But Stockport responded well, and thought they had levelled when Sidibeh raced through and found the net on 11 minutes. But he was deemed to have tripped George Johnston on the way through by VAR, and it was ruled out.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Kyle Wootton scored an unfortunate own goal during the match between Bolton and Stockport

Sidibeh was not to be denied again, however. On the half-hour mark he levelled with a smart header into the corner from Odin Bailey's inswinging cross.

Bolton rallied and retook the lead midway through the second half. A flash attack saw Cozier-Duberry's shot palmed by Addai into the path of Wootton, and the makeshift centre-back could not sort his feet out before steering it into the back of his own net.

And the win was sealed late on thanks to Dalby's acrobatic bicycle kick, and then through Rodrigues' late penalty, conceded by Dacres-Cogley, who was dismissed for pulling Ibrahim Cissoko's hair.

Schumacher: It's exactly what we deserve

Bolton boss Steven Schumacher speaking to Sky Sports:

"It was really difficult, especially in the first half, the heat and the conditions. I just said to the players at half-time, our intensity needs to be a bit higher with the ball and without the ball.

"If we can make a few more passes, tire Stockport out and get into the final third then we're in a position to create.

"Second half, I thought we were brilliant.

"It's all joy. Being a manager of Bolton Wanderers, that type of pressure is a privilege.

"I knew what I was getting into when I came to this football club. We've worked so hard, been here for 18 months now and everybody has pulled together to get us there.

"It's exactly what we deserve."

The key moment: 'Dalby introduction changed the game'

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Sam Dalby scores with an acrobatic overhead kick to extend Bolton's lead!

In the end it was the options off the bench that made the big difference, and the fact Steven Schumacher could turn to Dalby to bring on just after the hour mark.

Introduced with the game still deadlocked at 1-1, he provided crucial moments to turn the game in Bolton's favour.

Andy Hinchcliffe on Sky Sports Football:

"The Bolton players take all the glory because they go out and get the job done, but Steven Schumacher was brought to Bolton to provide promotion, to make it happen.

"There was huge pressure. This is a giant football club and he has done incredibly well.

"That decision to send on Sam Dalby, to take it from 1-1 to 3-1 changed the course of the game.

"Credit Dalby for his influence, but credit Schumacher for putting him on at just the right time."

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Stockport's Josh Dacres-Cogley sees red for hair pull and gives away penalty to seal Bolton's promotion

Lincoln boss Michael Skubala on Sky Sports Football:

"I think the timing of it was perfect. The heat was taking it out of the players, but it was a really attacking change and to get two No 9s onto the pitch up against Ethan Pye and Kyle Wootton, you can see how the game shifted.

"It was probably a little bit more direct, but it was what the game required.

"It took the game away from Stockport and, from there, there was only going to be one winner."

Sports.title: Fernandes breaks Premier League assists record
Sports.content:
Bruno Fernandes has broken the record for the most assists in a single Premier League season after the Manchester United captain set up Patrick Dorgu's goal against Brighton on the final day of the campaign.

It was Fernandes' 21st assist in the top flight this campaign, surpassing the record of 20 set by Thierry Henry for Arsenal in 2002/03 and Kevin De Bruyne for Manchester City in 2019/20.

Reporting on the match at the Amex Stadium, Sky Sports' David Richardson said: "History for Bruno! He has Dorgu to thank for getting free and powering a header in off the underside of the crossbar."

He matched the record in last weekend's 3-1 win against Nottingham Forest, setting up Bryan Mbeumo for Man Utd's third goal. He was named Premier League Player of the Season on Saturday, following on from his FWA Footballer of the Year award.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Bruno Fernandes beat David Beckham's record for the most assists in a single season for Manchester United - but which midfielder did it best?

Earlier this season, Fernandes broke David Beckham's record for the most assists provided for Manchester United in a single Premier League season, which was 15 in the 1999/2000 season.

But the 31-year-old is some way off the all-time Premier League assist record of 162 held by former Manchester United winger Ryan Giggs.

Most assists in PL history 162 - Ryan Giggs

119 - Kevin De Bruyne

111 - Cesc Fabregas

103 - Wayne Rooney

102 - Frank Lampard

More to follow...

Sports.title: Tottenham v Everton: Premier League final day – live
Sports.content:
now 12.17 EDT 49 min: … and doubly fortunately for Pickford, nothing comes of the resulting corner. Share

now 12.16 EDT 48 min: Spence cuts in from the right and aims for the bottom right. His shot is a dribbler, but Pickford, in an attempt to scoop it up, nearly shovels it into his own goal! The ball squirts inches wide of the right-hand post. Pickford blows out in relief. So close to a humiliating gaffe. Share

1m ago 12.15 EDT 47 min: Spence battles his way down the right and wins a corner off Mykolenko. The linesman – the same one with the knackered battery pack – doesn’t see the Everton man’s final touch, and awards a goal kick! That’s put the tin lid on it. The PGMOL, ladies and gentlemen. Share

4m ago 12.12 EDT Spurs finally get the second half started. Apart from the linesman’s battery pack, there have been no changes. Share

5m ago 12.12 EDT The West Ham v Leeds game has now reached the 51st minute. What nonsense. Share

5m ago 12.11 EDT Seems they were waiting to synchronise the second-half kick-off with the West Ham game. At which point the game at West Ham were given the go-ahead to start … only for this technical issue with the assistant referee to crop up. The fans whistle in irritation. This is a fiasco. Share

7m ago 12.10 EDT Spurs are left hanging for a minute or so by Everton, who emerge from the tunnel late, having presumably been given a full-fat bollocking for their first-half performance. They were abysmal. Then everyone has to wait while one of the linesman gets his walkie-talkie battery replaced. Dear me. Share

22m ago 11.55 EDT HALF TIME: West Ham United 0-0 Leeds United. So with Leeds holding the Hammers at the London Stadium, and with apologies to Simon McMahon’s liver (26 min), here’s the table AS IT STANDS. West Ham will be playing Championship football next season. Share

24m ago 11.53 EDT HALF TIME: Tottenham Hotspur 1-0 Everton A deserved lead for Spurs on the balance of play. Will it stop the nerves jangling in the second half? Of course it won’t! But the mood is a whole lot better since Palhinha headed against the post and rammed home the rebound. A whole lot better. Share

25m ago 11.51 EDT 45 min +5: Mykolenko requires some treatment after being caught late by Spence. But with the half-time whistle so close, he’s staying on, for now at least. Share

26m ago 11.51 EDT 45 min +3: The sub keeper Vicario is in a very strange mood this afternoon, incidentally. That row with Seamus Coleman, and now there’s footage of his celebrating the goal by taking De Zerbi in a headlock from behind. Share

27m ago 11.50 EDT 45 min +2: The stadium is now bouncing, by the way, like that’s breaking news given what’s just happened! Roberto De Zerbi reacted to the goal by wheeling around in a heightened state. Can you blame him? Share

28m ago 11.48 EDT 45 min +1: The first of four additional minutes. Share

29m ago 11.48 EDT 45 min: A long Everton throw comes in from the right. Bentancur barges into the back of Tarkowski, but though VAR has a quick look, there’s not going to be a penalty. Garner drags a poor shot wide right. Share

30m ago 11.47 EDT 44 min: That goal was a proper mess, but Spurs won’t care! Barry had hooked Palhinha’s shot from just behind the line. Danso followed it up, ramming home, but that’s Palhinha’s goal. Share

32m ago 11.45 EDT GOAL! Tottenham Hotspur 1-0 Everton (Palhinha 43) After a shaky few minutes, Spurs are finishing the half strongly … Richarlison dribbles down the left and wins an actual corner this time. Tel sends it to the far stick. Palhinha heads against the right-hand post. The rebound falls to him, and he pokes over the line. Bedlam! View image in fullscreen Photograph: Andrew Couldridge/Action Images/Reuters View image in fullscreen Joao Palhinha scores! Photograph: Andrew Matthews/PA Share Updated at 11.56 EDT

34m ago 11.43 EDT 41 min: Gallagher is going nowhere near the left-hand corner flag. But Rohl gifts him a free kick by needlessly barging into his back. A free kick that’s almost the same as a corner. Porro sends it long … and Pickford punches it clear likewise. Share

35m ago 11.42 EDT 40 min: Tel, just inside the Everton box on the left, drops a shoulder and looks for the top-right corner with a curler. It’s heading in, and it’s not clear that Pickford will get to it, so Tarkowski does exceptionally well to block. Tel spins around in frustration, suggesting he knew he’d hit a good one there, and the shot was on its way. Share

36m ago 11.40 EDT 38 min: Ndiaye wins the ball and makes good down the right. His cross is deflected into the air. Palhinha tries a weird back-flicked header across the face of his own box that nearly drops to Barry. He’s fortunate it doesn’t, and Everton clear their lines. Those anxiety levels are rising and rising. Share

39m ago 11.38 EDT 36 min: Rohl finds Dewsbury-Hall down the left. A ball’s slipped into the box along the channel in the hope of finding Barry. Kinsky claims. Everton are beginning to grow as an attacking force, albeit from a very low starting point. Share

40m ago 11.37 EDT 35 min: Palhinha romps down the inside-right channel and shoots. Deflection. Corner. The set piece is sent in, and Danso wins a free header on the penalty spot. He flaps a weak effort down and straight into the arms of Pickford. Spurs have had their chances. Danso has now had two of them. Will they end up regretting these misses? Share

41m ago 11.35 EDT 33 min: Dewsbury-Hall swings the corner into the six-yard box. Spurs let the ball sail all the way through. They’re fortunate that there’s nobody in blue to poke home. Eventually Spence clears. Audible anxiety as the volume dropped through all of that. Share

43m ago 11.34 EDT 32 min: Dewsbury-Hall tries a curler towards the top left from the right-hand edge of the Spurs box. It’s blocked. But Spurs come again, Ndiaye dribbling in from the right but not quite making enough space to get a shot away. He makes do with winning a cornner. From which … Share

45m ago 11.31 EDT 30 min: The xG so far: Spurs 0.38, Everton 0.03. Which tells quite a few stories, on both micro and macro levels. View image in fullscreen It’s all a bit cagey from both sides. Photograph: Vince Mignott/MB Media/Getty Images Share Updated at 11.38 EDT

47m ago 11.29 EDT 28 min: … though having said that, Everton have just spent a couple of minutes in Spurs territory, and there are a few frustrated groans from the home fans as a result. All of which will be music to the ears of David Moyes. Share

48m ago 11.28 EDT 27 min: Dewsbury-Hall advances down the left and wins a throw, which Mykolenko prepares to hoick long … but then throws short to Ndiaye. There goes another chance to dispatch the ball into the Spurs box. What on earth are Everton up to? Share

50m ago 11.27 EDT 26 min: The game restarts. “It’s partly cloudy and 20 degrees in Dundee, Scott, which qualifies as a heatwave in my book,” begins Simon McMahon. “Fear not, though, as I am having regular drinks breaks while watching the drama unfold, including a single malt every time the ‘as it stands’ table is shown. It’s been a long hard season, so why not? Good training for the World Cup too.” Hey, have a nippy sweetie on us. Share

51m ago 11.26 EDT 25 min: A drinks break, and it’s time for some tactical instruction as well. Roberto De Zerbi talking ten to the dozen. A lot of beneficial advice to impart. Share

52m ago 11.25 EDT 23 min: Spence gets the run on Mykolenko down the right. He crosses, hoping to find Richarlison in the middle for a tap-in. Pickford reads the danger and punches clear. Spurs looking far more dangerous than Everton, though that won’t stop the nerves jangling. Share

I didn’t support an English team growing up, but after moving back home to Iceland in 2010 after spending most of a decade in the US, my friend Ásgeir suggested I come with him every weekend to watch the Premier League. He was an Arsenal fan since childhood, and slowly but surely he converted me. This is the first league title they’ve won since then, but my friend, who I talked or messaged with during and after nearly every Arsenal game, passed away last year. So I’m sitting down now to watch with a Czech beer, his favourite tipple, to which he converted me too, and I’ll be thinking of the messages I would’ve been sending him. What a glorious day, nonetheless.” Beautiful message, Kari. A long time has passed since Arsenal’s last win, long enough I think for many Gunners fans to be negotiating similar emotions today.
